takeaway: Ulcerative colitis is associated with sclerosing cholangitis: jaundice with deranged liver tests in a patient with long-standing inflammatory bowel disease.

question.text: A 45-year-old woman has epigastric tenderness and jaundice. Her liver tests are deranged and she has a long history of inflammatory bowel disease. What is the likely diagnosis?
question.say: A forty-five-year-old woman has epigastric tenderness and jaundice. She has deranged liver biochemistry and a long history of inflammatory bowel disease. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.text: A woman with jaundice and a long scroll of IBD history.
lines.say: Here is a woman with jaundice and epigastric tenderness. Her scroll shows a long history of inflammatory bowel disease.

lines.text: Her liver tests are deranged: the paper shows arrows going up.
lines.say: Her liver biochemistry is deranged. The report in the liver's hand shows the numbers going up.

lines.text: The colon is the link: ulcerative colitis goes with sclerosing cholangitis.
lines.say: The colon is the link. Ulcerative colitis is associated with sclerosing cholangitis.

lines.text: The liver is tied up in knotted bile ducts: sclerosing cholangitis.
lines.say: (laugh) And look at the liver, all tied up in knotted bile ducts. That is sclerosing cholangitis.

lines.text: A long inflammatory bowel disease history is the big clue.
lines.say: So a long history of inflammatory bowel disease is the big clue.

lines.text: Remember: IBD with jaundice and deranged liver tests means sclerosing cholangitis.
lines.say: Remember: inflammatory bowel disease with jaundice and deranged liver tests suggests sclerosing cholangitis.
